answer: Clones of one operator tend to wake on one schedule, which lets an agent economy price keys by how their activity clusters in time. The ledger logs when each key answers, grades and mines; keys acting in shared 3-second windows in 8 of 10 epochs form a cohort, whose k-th member keeps 25×k² POA locked as a timber bond before its nectar, the epoch reward, can be withdrawn. Two keys lock 125, ten 9,625, and 1,000 need 8.4 billion, above the ~0.43M an epoch mints. A velvet review frees a flagged honest key that acts alone on a random prompt. Weakness: jitter hides cohorts but costs throughput.
